source.title: The Role of Linear Layers in Nonlinear Interpolating Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes how adding linear layers with weight decay changes interpolating functions and their behavior off the training support. Its theoretical results and numerical examples bear on architectural bias and generalization, but it does not measure held-out test error as the claim versions specify.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical representation-cost results and a numerical illustration of interpolants, but no held-out test-error measurements. The cited result about wider networks and generalization from Golubeva et al. (2020) is prior work, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: The study derives representation costs and illustrates how linear-layer depth changes ReLU interpolants. Its own results do not test any of V1–V8: it reports no relevant held-out performance comparison, convolutional versus fully connected comparison, or sharpness–generalization-gap analysis. The width–generalization result discussed in §1.1 is cited prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive representation costs reflecting an interplay between ReLU-unit alignment and outer-layer sparsity, favoring low-dimensional projections admitting parsimonious interpolants. Alignment alone does not determine the preferred interpolant. Improved out-of-distribution generalization is suggested as a possibility, not measured.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives representation-cost results for networks with linear layers followed by a ReLU layer and illustrates interpolating functions trained with SGD and weight decay. It does not reproduce the claim versions' held-out test-error experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The preferred representation cost can depend on the training data geometry, angle between rays, outer-layer weight balance, and choice of projection subspace; Figure 2 shows aligned units need not minimize the cost in every setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Additional linear layers change minimum representation costs through both ReLU-unit alignment and outer-layer sparsity. Numerical interpolants illustrate alignment with increasing depth; theoretical and two-ray examples show that aligned units need not have lower representation cost.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-representation-cost ReLU interpolation with additional linear layers favors low-dimensional projections that admit parsimonious interpolants, with preferences depending on data geometry and outer-layer weights.

record.problems: The examples are illustrative surface plots and do not report held-out test error or quantitative uncertainty. The paper's theoretical results concern representation costs and interpolant behavior, so their implications for generalization are not directly measured.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The text cites Golubeva et al. (2020) on width and generalization, but that is prior work and is excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding held-out performance on natural and random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance, local connectivity, and initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning and weight-decay recipes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including training-set size, dropout strength, and data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: V3's tested_not_extracted status should be changed to not_tested. Representation cost and off-support function geometry do not establish any listed version's held-out generalization effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural or random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error as a function of width.
The study compares linear-layer depth effects within ReLU networks, not convolutional versus fully connected classifiers or their test errors.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, and comparison with other measures.
Removal of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.
